He was known for his unusual build as a basketball player, stockier than most small forwards, yet shorter than most power forwards he faced. However, Barkley was still capable of outplaying both taller and quicker opponents because of his unusual combination of strength and agility.[[7]](#cite_note-nbaob-8)

Barkley was a prolific scorer who averaged 22.1 points per game during the regular season for his career and 23.0 points per game in the playoffs for his career. Barkley was an incredibly efficient offensive force, leading the NBA in 2-point field goal percentage every season from the 1986–87 season to the 1990–91 season. He led the league in effective field goal percentage in both the 1986–87 and 1987–88 seasons as well, and also led the league in offensive rating in both the 1988–89 and 1989–90 seasons.[[33]](#cite_note-cbcstats-34) He was one of the NBA's most versatile players and accurate scorers capable of scoring from anywhere on the court and established himself as one of the NBA's premier [clutch](/wiki/Clutch_(sports) "Clutch (sports)") players.[[7]](#cite_note-nbaob-8) During his NBA career, Barkley was a constant mismatch because he possessed a very uncommon combination of skills and could play in a variety of positions. The Labrador is an exceptionally popular dog. As of 2006, it was widely considered one of the most popular dog breeds, and it is the most popular dog by ownership in Canada, New Zealand[[45]](#cite_note-46) and the United Kingdom.[[46]](#cite_note-47) In 2006, in both the United Kingdom and the United States, there were well over twice as many registered Labradors as the next most popular breed.[[47]](#cite_note-uk_kc_stats-48)[[48]](#cite_note-akc_stats-49) If the comparison is limited to dog breeds of a similar size, then there are around 3–5 times as many Labradors registered in both countries as the next most popular breeds, the [German Shepherd](/wiki/German_Shepherd "German Shepherd") and the Golden Retriever.[[47]](#cite_note-uk_kc_stats-48)[[48]](#cite_note-akc_stats-49)

Labs are the most popular breed of [assistance dog](/wiki/Assistance_dog "Assistance dog") in the United States, Australia and many other countries,[[49]](#cite_note-Alecia-50) as well as being widely used by police and other official bodies for their detection and working abilities. Approximately 60–70% of all guide dogs in the United States are Labradors.

In 2022 Labrador Retrievers were the second-most-popular breed in the United States.[[50]](#cite_note-51) In 2020 the Labrador was the most popular registered dog breed in New Zealand.[[51]](#cite_note-52)

Seven out of the thirteen "outstanding [gundogs](/wiki/Gundog "Gundog")" of the [Australian National Kennel Council](/wiki/Australian_National_Kennel_Council "Australian National Kennel Council")'s 2000–05 appointees to its 'hall of fame' are Labradors.[[52]](#cite_note-53)

James Francis Cameron[[7]](#cite_note-7) was born on August 16, 1954, in [Kapuskasing](/wiki/Kapuskasing "Kapuskasing"), Ontario, to Philip Cameron, an [electrical engineer](/wiki/Electrical_engineer "Electrical engineer"), and Shirley ([née](/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Lowe), an artist and nurse.[[8]](#cite_note-nytimesref-8) He is the first of five children, with two brothers and two sisters.[[8]](#cite_note-nytimesref-8) His paternal great-great-great-grandfather emigrated from [Balquhidder](/wiki/Balquhidder "Balquhidder"), Scotland, in 1825.[[8]](#cite_note-nytimesref-8) Cameron spent summers on his grandfather's farm in [Southern Ontario](/wiki/Southern_Ontario "Southern Ontario").[[9]](#cite_note-9) He attended Stamford Collegiate in [Niagara Falls, Ontario](/wiki/Niagara_Falls,_Ontario "Niagara Falls, Ontario"). At age 17, Cameron and his family moved from [Chippawa, Ontario](/wiki/Chippawa,_Ontario "Chippawa, Ontario") to [Brea, California](/wiki/Brea,_California "Brea, California").[[10]](#cite_note-10) He attended [Sonora High School](/wiki/Sonora_High_School_(La_Habra,_California) "Sonora High School (La Habra, California)") and then moved to [Brea Olinda High School](/wiki/Brea_Olinda_High_School "Brea Olinda High School"). Classmates recalled that he was not a sportsman but instead enjoyed building things that "either went up into the air or into the deep".[[11]](#cite_note-11)

After high school, Cameron enrolled at [Fullerton College](/wiki/Fullerton_College "Fullerton College"), a community college, in 1973 to study physics. He switched subjects to English, but left the college at the end of 1974.[[12]](#cite_note-12) Cameron worked odd jobs, including as a truck driver and a high school janitor. London School of Economics :: History :: Origins :: chunk_0002
The London School of Economics and Political Science was founded in 1895[[13]](#cite_note-LSEHistoryAbout-13) by [Beatrice](/wiki/Beatrice_Webb "Beatrice Webb") and [Sidney Webb](/wiki/Sidney_Webb,_1st_Baron_Passfield "Sidney Webb, 1st Baron Passfield"), [Graham Wallas](/wiki/Graham_Wallas "Graham Wallas") and [George Bernard Shaw](/wiki/George_Bernard_Shaw "George Bernard Shaw")[[14]](#cite_note-LSEHistoryWebbs-14) initially funded by a bequest of £20,000[[15]](#cite_note-SpartacusLSE-15)[[16]](#cite_note-Statisticians-16) from the [estate](/wiki/Estate_(law) "Estate (law)") of Henry Hunt Hutchinson. Hutchinson, a lawyer[[15]](#cite_note-SpartacusLSE-15) and member of the [Fabian Society](/wiki/Fabian_Society "Fabian Society"),[[17]](#cite_note-SmithLSEandEducation-17)[[18]](#cite_note-LSEPassfieldArchives-18) left the money in trust, to be put "towards advancing its [The Fabian Society's] objects in any way they [the [trustees](/wiki/Trustee "Trustee")] deem advisable".[[18]](#cite_note-LSEPassfieldArchives-18) The five trustees were Sidney Webb, [Edward Pease](/wiki/Edward_R._Pease "Edward R. Pease"), Constance Hutchinson, [W. S. de Mattos](/wiki/W._S._de_Mattos "W. S. de Mattos") and William Clark.[[15]](#cite_note-SpartacusLSE-15)

LSE records that the proposal to establish the school was conceived during a breakfast meeting on 4 August 1894, between the Webbs, Louis Flood, and [George Bernard Shaw](/wiki/George_Bernard_Shaw "George Bernard Shaw").[[13]](#cite_note-LSEHistoryAbout-13) The proposal was accepted by the trustees in February 1895[[18]](#cite_note-LSEPassfieldArchives-18) and LSE held its first classes in October of that year, in rooms at 9 John Street, [Adelphi](/wiki/Adelphi,_London "Adelphi, London"),[[19]](#cite_note-LSEHistory1895-19) in the [City of Westminster](/wiki/City_of_Westminster "City of Westminster").

fanoutqa_021674.x:
Nippon Professional Baseball :: History :: Expansion and contraction :: chunk_0006
The Central League's [Nishi Nippon Pirates](/wiki/Nishi_Nippon_Pirates "Nishi Nippon Pirates") existed for one season—they placed sixth in 1950, and the following season merged with the [Nishitetsu Clippers](/wiki/Nishitetsu_Clippers "Nishitetsu Clippers") (also based in Fukuoka) to form the [Nishitetsu Lions](/wiki/Nishitetsu_Lions "Nishitetsu Lions"). This brought the number of Central League teams down to an ungainly arrangement of seven. In 1952, it was decided that any Central League team ending the season with a winning percentage below .300 would be disbanded or merged with other teams. The [Shochiku Robins](/wiki/Shochiku_Robins "Shochiku Robins") fell into this category, and were merged with the [Taiyō Whales](/wiki/Taiy%C5%8D_Whales "Taiyō Whales") to become the [Taiyō Shochiku Robins](/wiki/Taiy%C5%8D_Shochiku_Robins "Taiyō Shochiku Robins") in January 1953. This enabled the Central League to shrink to an even number of six teams.

In 1954 a new [Pacific League](/wiki/Pacific_League "Pacific League") team was founded, the [Takahashi Unions](/wiki/Takahashi_Unions "Takahashi Unions"), to increase the number of teams in that division to eight. Although the team was stocked with players from the other Pacific League teams, the Unions struggled from the outset and finished in the second division every season. In 1957, the Unions were merged with the [Daiei Stars](/wiki/Daiei_Stars "Daiei Stars") to form the [Daiei Unions](/wiki/Daiei_Unions "Daiei Unions") (and again bringing the number of Pacific League teams down to seven). The Unions existed for a single season, finishing in last place, 43-1/2 games out of first. In 1958, the Unions merged with the [Mainichi Orions](/wiki/Mainichi_Orions "Mainichi Orions") to form the [Daimai Orions](/wiki/Daimai_Orions "Daimai Orions"). This enabled the Pacific League to contract from the ungainly seven-team arrangement to six teams.

Born on the island of [Corsica](/wiki/Corsica "Corsica") to a family of Italian origin, Napoleon moved to mainland France in 1779 and was commissioned as an officer in the [French Royal Army](/wiki/French_Royal_Army "French Royal Army") in 1785. He supported the French Revolution in 1789 and promoted its cause in Corsica. He rose rapidly through the ranks after winning the [siege of Toulon](/wiki/Siege_of_Toulon_(1793) "Siege of Toulon (1793)") in 1793 and defeating royalist insurgents in Paris on [13 Vendémiaire](/wiki/13_Vend%C3%A9miaire "13 Vendémiaire") in 1795. In 1796, he commanded [a military campaign](/wiki/Italian_campaign_of_1796%E2%80%931797 "Italian campaign of 1796–1797") against the [Austrians](/wiki/Habsburg_monarchy "Habsburg monarchy") and their Italian allies in the [War of the First Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_First_Coalition "War of the First Coalition"), scoring decisive victories and becoming a national hero. He led an [invasion of Egypt and Syria](/wiki/French_invasion_of_Egypt_and_Syria "French invasion of Egypt and Syria") in 1798, which served as a springboard to political power. In November 1799, Napoleon engineered the [Coup of 18 Brumaire](/wiki/Coup_of_18_Brumaire "Coup of 18 Brumaire") against the [French Directory](/wiki/French_Directory "French Directory") and became First Consul of the Republic. He won the [Battle of Marengo](/wiki/Battle_of_Marengo "Battle of Marengo") in 1800, which secured France's victory in the [War of the Second Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Second_Coalition "War of the Second Coalition"), and in 1803, he [sold the territory of Louisiana](/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase") to the United States. In December 1804, Napoleon [crowned himself](/wiki/Coronation_of_Napoleon "Coronation of Napoleon") Emperor of the French, further expanding his power.
